extracted.intended_audience: readers of The New Republic and the general public interested in the Beauchamp/Army controversy and investigative journalism
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial update describing The New Republic's ongoing investigation into alleged inaccuracies in a previously published diary piece by Scott Beauchamp, explaining the paper's evidentiary standards, interactions with sources and the Army, and its approach to potential retraction or correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: uncover the truth before action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Since this controversy began, The New Republic’s sole objective has been to uncover the truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not retract or confirm a story until the truth is established; the paper will retract only if parts are proven false and will stand by the piece if proven true. The phrasing emphasizes that editorial decisions (such as retraction) should be driven strictly by evidentiary certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction policy tied to evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it's certain parts of the story are bullshit, then we'll end that way. If it's proven to be true, it will end that way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A retraction is warranted only when conclusive documentary or testimonial evidence proves fabrication/embellishment. Conversely, verification supports keeping the piece. This frames retraction as contingent on demonstrable proof rather than public pressure or leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration as key evaluative standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier reporting had "uncovered significant evidence corroborating Beauchamp's accounts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent corroborating evidence strengthens the credibility of contested claims and is a primary reason to continue treating the piece as potentially valid while further investigation proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source willingness and ability to defend claims matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauchamp's refusal to discuss his article raised serious doubts; later he told editors he stood by every aspect except a previously admitted inaccuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subject's refusal to engage or to defend their reporting is a substantive factor in assessing credibility, but subsequent unmonitored affirmations or denials (and their conditions) must be considered in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context of statements (monitoring/duress) affects reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauchamp spoke on September 6 with his squad leader and a public affairs specialist in the room and later said he had spoken under duress and that the Army was recording the conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate statements made under monitoring or possible coercion with caution; interrogate whether a statement was made freely or under pressure, as that affects its evidentiary weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and completeness of rival investigations matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Cross conceded he had not interviewed at least a dozen soldiers in Beauchamp's platoon; the Army investigation 'got statements from everyone in his platoon that was available that day' but did not follow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess conclusions of an institutional investigation by checking whether all relevant witnesses were interviewed and whether follow-up occurred; gaps undermine claims of conclusiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary documentary records and FOIA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: TNR filed a FOIA request for all documents pertaining to the Army's investigation and repeatedly requested documents directly from the First Infantry Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek primary documents (investigative statements, transcripts) through formal channels (FOIA) rather than relying on summaries or selective disclosures. Documentary evidence is prioritized for establishing facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about selective leaks and secondary reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army leaked selective parts of the record to bloggers; Drudge Report incorrectly reported that documents showed Beauchamp had recanted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat leaked or selectively released documents, and reports based on them, with skepticism until the full record is obtained and independently examined. Beware of misinterpretation or overreach by secondary outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about investigative process and delays
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors explain delays: FOIA review timing, difficulties obtaining documents, and the Army's behavior; they state an obligation to deliver a full account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform readers about the status of an investigation, reasons for delays, and steps being taken. Transparency about process builds trust and explains why editorial actions (or lack thereof) occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respecting subjects' access constraints and institutional control of records
rubrics_metrics.description: When Beauchamp requested his own statements he was told he had to coordinate dissemination with Army public affairs; statements could be released only through FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize institutional restrictions on documentary access and pursue appropriate legal/administrative channels; note when subjects are impeded from obtaining or sharing evidence, as that bears on transparency and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for prior corrections or admitted inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauchamp stood by every aspect of his story 'except for the one inaccuracy he had previously admitted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a subject has previously admitted an inaccuracy, incorporate that admission into the assessment (make corrections where appropriate) while separately evaluating other unadmitted claims for corroboration.
